title: Rigveda 10.148: To Indra
source: Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 48 (1711 CE (colophon: Saṃvat 1768)), OPenn, Public Domain Mark + Aufrecht's accented text (GRETIL) + Griffith's English (VedaWeb)
description: Rigveda 10.148: To Indra: Sanskrit text and Griffith's English, each verse linked to the page of a 1711 Rigveda manuscript (Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 48) that carries it.
introduction:
Rigveda 10.148 is a hymn of 5 verses addressed to Indra. It stands in book (maṇḍala) 10, the last and latest book. The Rigveda is the oldest collection of Sanskrit hymns, composed in the second half of the second millennium BCE and handed down orally for many centuries before it was written down.

The manuscript shown is Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 48 (University of Pennsylvania), a paper manuscript of the eighth aṣṭaka (RV 10.46-10.191) of the Ṛgveda Saṃhitā in Devanāgarī, 158 leaves, 6 lines to the page, with the accents marked in red; the scribe's colophon on fol. 158 gives Saṃvat 1768 (1711 CE); this hymn stands on fol. 133r-133v. Each section below gives the verses that end on one page; the page boundaries were read on the images (the opening words of every page), not counted out. Like most Rigveda manuscripts, Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 48 writes a repeated refrain in short form after its first occurrence (for example kasmai° for kasmai devāya haviṣā vidhema); the Sanskrit shown is the full text of Aufrecht's edition.
translator_notes: Sanskrit: Aufrecht's edition (1877) with the Vedic accents, as entered by van Nooten and Holland (GRETIL).

English: Ralph T. H. Griffith, The Hymns of the Rigveda (1889-1892; 2nd ed. 1896-1897), from the VedaWeb digital text; OCR slips in that text were corrected against the printed 2nd edition (data/sources/rigveda/griffith_errata.json).

translation.original_ref: RV 10.148.1-2 (aṣṭaka 8, adhyāya 8, varga 6); Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 48 fol. 133r
translation.original_text:
1su̱ṣvā̱ṇāsa̍ indra stu̱masi̍ tvā sasa̱vāṁsa̍ś ca tuvinṛmṇa̱ vāja̍m | ā no̍ bhara suvi̱taṁ yasya̍ cā̱kan tmanā̱ tanā̍ sanuyāma̱ tvotā̍ḥ ||
2ṛ̱ṣvas tvam i̍ndra śūra jā̱to dāsī̱r viśa̱ḥ sūrye̍ṇa sahyāḥ | guhā̍ hi̱taṁ guhya̍ṁ gū̱ḻham a̱psu bi̍bhṛ̱masi̍ pra̱srava̍ṇe̱ na soma̍m ||
translation.text:
1WHEN we have pressed the juice we laud thee, Indra, and when, Most Valorous we have won the booty. Bring us prosperity, as each desires it under thine own protection may we conquer.
2Sublime from birth, mayst thou O Indra, Hero, with Sûrya overcome the Dâsa races. As by a fountain's side, we bring the Soma that lay concealed, close-hidden in the waters.
translation.scan_note: Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 48, fol. 133r (OPenn image 132, lower leaf). Checked on the image: the Rigveda text on this page begins in RV 10.147.4 ‹vājam bharate dhanā nṛbhiḥ›. The next page with Rigveda text, fol. 133v, begins in RV 10.148.3 ‹-enota tubhyaṁ rathoḻha bhakṣaiḥ›. Verses 10.148.1-2 end on this page.

translation.original_ref: RV 10.148.3-5 (aṣṭaka 8, adhyāya 8, varga 6); Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 48 fol. 133v
translation.original_text:
3a̱ryo vā̱ giro̍ a̱bhy a̍rca vi̱dvān ṛṣī̍ṇā̱ṁ vipra̍ḥ suma̱tiṁ ca̍kā̱naḥ | te syā̍ma̱ ye ra̱ṇaya̍nta̱ somai̍r e̱nota tubhya̍ṁ rathoḻha bha̱kṣaiḥ ||
4i̱mā brahme̍ndra̱ tubhya̍ṁ śaṁsi̱ dā nṛbhyo̍ nṛ̱ṇāṁ śū̍ra̱ śava̍ḥ | tebhi̍r bhava̱ sakra̍tu̱r yeṣu̍ cā̱kann u̱ta trā̍yasva gṛṇa̱ta u̱ta stīn ||
5śru̱dhī hava̍m indra śūra̱ pṛthyā̍ u̱ta sta̍vase ve̱nyasyā̱rkaiḥ | ā yas te̱ yoni̍ṁ ghṛ̱tava̍nta̱m asvā̍r ū̱rmir na nimnair dra̍vayanta̱ vakvā̍ḥ ||
translation.text:
3Answer the votary's hymns, for these thou knowest, craving the R̥ishis' prayer, thyself a Singer May we be they who take delight in Somas: these with sweet food for thee, O Chariot-rider.
4These holy prayers, O Indra, have I sung thee: grant to the men the strength of men, thou Hero. Be of one mind with those in whom thou joyest: keep thou the singers safe and their companions.
5Listen to Pr̥ithî's call, heroic Indra, and be thou lauded by the hymns of Venya, Him who hath sung thee to thine oil-rich dwelling, whose rolling songs have sped thee like a torrent.
translation.scan_note: Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 48, fol. 133v (OPenn image 133, upper leaf). Checked on the image: the Rigveda text on this page begins in RV 10.148.3 ‹-enota tubhyaṁ rathoḻha bhakṣaiḥ›. The next page with Rigveda text, fol. 134r, begins in RV 10.149.2 ‹dyāvāpṛthivī aprathetām›. Verses 10.148.3-5 end on this page; 10.148.3 begins on fol. 133r.
